subject: MAP: Pilot performance evaluation & concurrency gating for NovaHealth
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>

Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>

Subject: MAP: Pilot performance evaluation & concurrency gating for NovaHealth

Hi Iliana / Rahul —

Thanks again for the time on Friday. Per our call I’ve sketched a focused MAP + evaluation plan to validate performance (latency, throughput, TTFT) and concurrency behavior before pilot kickoff. Please review and confirm so we can lock dates. High-level summary below; full MAP attached ([attachment: q3_map.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]).

Objectives:
- Validate steady-state throughput and latency targets for your main inference route (chat-completion style workload).
- Characterize burst behaviour (burst vs steady-state), queueing thresholds, and failover behavior when capacity is saturated.
- Measure TTFT (time-to-first-token) and tail latency (p95, p99) at targeted concurrency.

Proposed test plan (short):
1) Dataset & prompts — Iliana to confirm the representative prompt set (20k tokens total, 200 prompts across categories). (Owner: NovaHealth; due: 2025-07-17)
2) Baseline run — steady-state ramp to target RPS (10k tokens/min) and hold 30 minutes. Collect p50/p95/p99 and TTFT. (Owner: Redwood - Laura; scheduled: 2025-07-21 02:00 UTC)
3) Burst tests — simulate sudden spikes (2x, 5x, 10x) for 2 minutes each; measure queueing, rate-limited responses, and error rates. (Owner: Redwood - Laura; scheduled: 2025-07-21 03:00 UTC)
4) Concurrency sweep — increase concurrent streams from 1 to 256, measure per-stream latency and throughput, identify queuing onset and max sustainable concurrency. (Owner: Redwood - Laura; scheduled: 2025-07-21 04:00 UTC)
5) Tuned rerun — apply rate-limit and batching recommendations, rerun key tests to show improved stability. (Owner: Redwood - Laura/Ben; scheduled: 2025-07-22)

Success criteria (examples):
- TTFT < 220ms p50, p95 < 350ms at target workload; p99 < 750ms or documented fallback behaviour.
- No more than 1% 5xx errors during steady-state.
- Graceful queueing (retry headers, 429 with Retry-After) during bursts; documented recommended throttles.

Proposed MAP close timeline: pilot decision by 2025-07-30; contract sign by 2025-08-07. If you want to accelerate, we can compress the test window next week.

Next steps: please confirm prompt set ownership and approve the test window. I’ll loop in Laura and Monica to execute tests and capture the report.

Thanks,
Ben

Hi Iliana / Ben —

We ran the compressed test window yesterday (17 Jul) and I’m attaching the raw latency export and a short summary (attached: latency_results.csv, burst_vs_steady_summary.pdf). Key findings below — I focused on reproducible thresholds and recommended tuning for the pilot.

Executive summary:
- Steady-state (15k tokens/min, ~110 concurrent streams by our generator config): TTFT p50 = 190ms, p95 = 310ms, p99 = 680ms. Sustained 15k tokens/min with <0.5% 5xx.
- Burst behavior: 2x spike (30k tokens/min) caused increased p95 to ~520ms and p99 to ~1.4s, but <1% 5xx and service returned to baseline within 75s after spike end. 5x spike behavior showed queueing onset and saw 429s with Retry-After headers when the internal queue reached configured max_concurrency.
- Concurrency sweep: per-stream latency begins degrading noticeably after ~160 concurrent streams in our setup; queue depth increases and we observed a sharp p99 cliff after 200 concurrent streams.

Detailed observations and recommendations:
1) Queueing behavior: Redis-backed request queue reached configured soft_limit (~180) before hard limit; once soft limit hit, we saw increases in TTFT due to requests queued in front of KV cache population. Recommendation: set soft_limit to 150 for pilot and enable token-based backpressure (client-side token bucket) to smooth bursts.
2) Rate-limit tuning: For your workload we recommend a per-route rate_limit of 18k tokens/min with burst token allowance of 1.5x sustained. Combine with client-side Retry-After handling set to exponential backoff starting at 500ms.
3) Batching & KV cache: Increase max_batch_size to 32 for high-concurrency paths and enable aggressive KV cache warmup (prepopulate common prompts) — this reduced median token rendering time by ~20% in our runs.
4) Fallbacks: Configure automatic fallback to lower-capacity model variant at >2% sustained 5xx or when queue depth > soft_limit for >60s. This preserves availability while protecting tail quality.

Attached are the CSVs and a 2-page PDF with graphs. Let me know if you want a walkthrough and we can schedule a 30-min call to walk through the plots.

Attachments: [latency_results.csv (text/csv)], [burst_vs_steady_summary.pdf (application/pdf)]
